Definition: of Latin origin; Gallion (i.e. Gallio), a Roman officer:--Gallio.
BiblicalUsage: Gallio was the deputy of Achaia, the Roman proconsul before whom the Jews brought Paul in Acts 18:12. They accused Paul of persuading men to worship God contrary to the law, and when Paul was about to speak, Gallio said in Acts 18:14 that if it were a matter of wrong or wicked lewdness, he would bear with them — but this was a matter of words and names, and he drove them from the judgment seat.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Gallio's refusal is a small mercy in the book of Acts. A Roman governor would not judge the gospel, and Paul went on his way unharmed; I hold that God can use even a careless judge to protect His servants.
